overall: Atlanta is starting June 21st under a surprisingly deep overcast (OVC, 100% cloud cover, ceiling at only ~400ft/122m), which has kept temperatures essentially flat all night and through 9:20 AM at 73.4°F running max — well below the trajectory needed for an 88°F high. Warming velocity is stalled at 0.0°F/hr, and despite a humid dewpoint near 70°F, there is no meaningful heating underway yet. The NWS 'mostly sunny' narrative is in direct conflict with current overcast reality, which is the dominant feature of this morning.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models (ECMWF 86.0°F, HRRR 85.2°F, NBM 86.4°F) cluster tightly around 85–86°F and all sit below the NWS narrative high of 88°F — that modest gap likely reflects the models' partial accounting of the morning cloud deck. The META (fused) model's top bucket is 86–87°F at 36.9%, aligning closely with the NWP consensus, while the intraday obs-driven model skews slightly warmer (88–89°F at 24.2%) but was built before this prolonged overcast became fully apparent.
max_temp_prediction: The persistent OVC deck with a very low ceiling will delay the onset of solar heating by several hours, robbing the day of its peak insolation window and making the NWS 88°F target a stretch. If the overcast breaks by noon as the NWS implies, there is still enough afternoon time (models peak ~16.7h ET) to reach the upper 85–87°F range, but any further delay in clearing pushes the outcome toward the mid-80s. Best estimate is approximately 86.5°F, reflecting the NWP consensus, the META model's modal bucket of 86–87°F, and a moderate downside bias from the anomalously deep morning cloud cover; confidence is moderate-low given the unresolved clearing timeline.
